subject.title: [Feature]: Global (IP-agnostic) auth rate limiting option for public-exposed deployments

question: Should Gateway auth support a permanent default-off IP-agnostic failed-auth lockout mode for public token/password deployments?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested config changes the Gateway auth security boundary and intentionally allows all-client lockout under attack, so automation should not choose the product/security policy.

options.title: Accept after security fixes
options.body: Proceed with a default-off core config mode only after the linked PR fixes the known security/docs gaps and posts real Gateway proof.

options.title: Keep mitigation outside core
options.body: Reject the new core knob and document identity-aware proxy or external brute-force controls for public deployments instead.

options.title: Defer into broader hardening
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers settle wider public-exposure hardening, including password strength and rate-limit policy.

recommendation.title: Accept after security fixes
recommendation.body: Proceed with a default-off core config mode only after the linked PR fixes the known security/docs gaps and posts real Gateway proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest individual history signal on this Gateway auth rate-limit policy surface and the path is secops-owned by CODEOWNERS.
